name: Ichibancho and Kokubuncho
tagline: Arcade shopping by day, Tohoku's biggest nightlife by night
description: Central Aoba ward is built around covered shopping arcades that keep you dry in rain and snow, with department stores, chain cafes and independent kissaten stacked along them. One street west, Kokubuncho turns into the largest entertainment district north of Tokyo, packed with izakaya and bars.
bestFor: Nomads who want everything walkable and do not mind paying central rents for it.
pros: Covered arcades make winter errands easy
Huge choice of cafes and restaurants
cons: Kokubuncho gets loud late on weekends
Older buildings can be small and thin-walled

name: Sendai Station East Side
tagline: Newer towers a footbridge from the shinkansen
description: The Higashiguchi side of Sendai Station has been rebuilt over the last decade with newer apartment towers, supermarkets and chain restaurants. It is flatter and cheaper than the west side, and a covered footbridge drops you straight onto the shinkansen platforms for trips to Tokyo in 90 minutes.
bestFor: Nomads who travel out of Sendai often and want new-build comfort near the station.
pros: Walking distance to shinkansen and all rail lines
Newer apartment stock with better insulation
Cheaper than the arcade side of the station
cons: Less charm, mostly new blocks and car parks
Fewer independent cafes than central Aoba
Traffic noise near the main roads

name: Kawauchi and Tohoku University
tagline: Campus greenery on the Hirose river bend
description: West of the river below the old castle site, Kawauchi holds Tohoku University campuses, the art museum and long stretches of riverside path. Student housing keeps rents down, cheap set-lunch places line the approach roads, and the tree cover here is what earned Sendai its City of Trees nickname.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads who want green space, cheap food and an international student crowd.
pros: Most international crowd in the city
cons: Quiet and half-empty during university holidays
Hilly walk up from the river
Limited evening options, most people head into town

name: Nagamachi
tagline: Malls, family flats and a ten-minute subway ride in
description: Taihaku ward's main hub sits two rail lines south of the centre, with large shopping malls, a hospital and rows of mid-rise family apartments around Nagamachi-Minami. Rents run well below central Aoba, and both the subway and the JR line reach Sendai Station in under ten minutes.
bestFor: Couples or longer stays wanting more square metres for the money.
pros: Two rail options into the city
Big supermarkets and malls on the doorstep
cons: Little nightlife without going into town

name: Izumi-Chuo
tagline: A planned northern sub-centre with parks and space
description: The terminus of the Namboku subway line, Izumi-Chuo was laid out as a satellite centre with wide streets, a stadium, parks and shopping complexes. Families dominate, apartments are larger, and the mountains start just behind, though you are roughly 20 minutes of subway from the arcades.
bestFor: Nomads staying months who value quiet, space and easy access to the hills.
pros: Parks, sports facilities and clean air
Direct subway to the city centre
cons: Very little going on in the evenings
Colder and snowier than the city core
